kurz: Which state taxes foreign income first, which part of that tax can be credited in Germany, and what applies when no German bank withholds tax.

bloecke.md:
As long as everything stays within Germany, the German flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) is convenient. The bank does the settlement and transfers the tax to the tax office; nothing else needs to be done. If a portfolio has a foreign connection, this process breaks down at three points. First, the state from which the income originates levies its tax first, that is, before Germany. Second, German tax deduction does not take place at all if the institution holding the securities account is not based in Germany. Third, moving away from Germany can itself trigger a taxable event without a single security being sold.

The three cases are not related in substance, but all of them are underestimated.

## Withholding tax and crediting

If a US company pays a dividend to a German investor, the US withholds 30% by law. The double taxation agreement between Germany and the US limits the tax deduction to 15%. German custodian banks usually apply this rate automatically at source using form W-8BEN. The US receives this 15%, and it stays there.

So that the same income is not taxed in full twice, Germany credits the foreign tax. Under Section 32d(5) EStG (Income Tax Act), the credit is at most 25% per individual item of capital income, and only as much as the relevant agreement allows the source state, usually 15%. The credit is applied to each item of income individually, not to the net total for the year. It reduces the capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) itself (Section 32d(1) sentence 2 EStG). The German custodian bank already takes care of this when deducting tax. For this purpose, it keeps a third pot for creditable withholding tax alongside the two loss pots.

bloecke.formel: Creditable = min(Withholding tax paid, DTA maximum rate, 25% × Income)
bloecke.erklaerung: The German tax office does not take into account any withholding tax deducted in excess of this amount. That excess can only be reclaimed in the source state.
variablen: the withholding tax rate agreed in the relevant double taxation agreement (DTA), usually 15%
the individual item of capital income, not the annual total
bloecke.beispiel: From a Swiss dividend of €1,000, €350 is withheld, and €150 is creditable. The difference of €200 can only be recovered through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration.

bloecke.md:
The credit reduces the capital income withholding tax, and the solidarity surcharge is based on the reduced capital income withholding tax. Instead of 5.5% on €250, only 5.5% on €100 is therefore due. The total burden falls from 26.375% to 25.55%.

The advantage arises solely from the method of calculation, amounts to around €8 per €1,000 of dividends and is not a tax planning model. Compared with the other influences on the investment result, it is too small to be a reason for selecting shares by their country of domicile.

bloecke.titel: Swiss dividend of €1,000 gross without reclaim
bloecke.unter: The €200 above the treaty rate does not concern the German tax procedure and does not appear in any German tax return.

bloecke.md:
The saver's allowance is applied to the gross income before any tax arises. If the exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) fully covers a US dividend of €800, no German tax is due on it. The bank then records the €120 of US withholding tax in the withholding tax pot and credits it against flat-rate withholding tax that arises on other capital income in the same year. If no German flat-rate withholding tax arises in the whole year, there is no tax against which it could be credited, and it is lost for good. With a German dividend of the same amount, the full €800 would have remained tax-free.

A filled loss pot has the same effect. In addition, unlike the loss pots, the withholding tax pot is not carried forward to the following year. It is closed on 31 December, and the investor can only offset any remainder in the tax return for the same year against flat-rate withholding tax on income at other banks.

## Withholding tax leakage in funds

With funds and ETFs, withholding tax is incurred at fund level, not by the investor. Since the 2018 investment tax reform, private investors can no longer credit it personally, not even through the capital income annex (Anlage KAP). This is compensated for on a flat-rate basis through the [[Partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)|partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)]]. It is 30% for equity funds, 15% for mixed funds and 60% or 80% for real estate funds with a domestic or foreign focus, as set out in Section 20 InvStG (Investment Tax Act).

How high the burden is depends on the fund domicile, which can be recognised from the prefix of the ISIN. An ETF domiciled in Ireland pays 15% US withholding tax thanks to the Irish-US agreement, whereas a physically replicating fund from Luxembourg pays the full 30%. Ireland itself does not levy withholding tax on distributions to non-resident investors. Investors will not find the difference shown anywhere. It reduces the net asset value and appears neither in the cost ratio nor in the tax certificate.

bloecke.formel: Leakage in percentage points p.a. ≈ US index weight × Dividend yield × Withholding tax rate
bloecke.erklaerung: The formula gives an order of magnitude, not an exact figure, because the dividend yield and the index composition fluctuate.
bloecke.beispiel: For the MSCI World, with a US weighting of around 73% and a dividend yield of roughly 1.1% in the US part (end of September 2026), the result is 0.73 × 1.1% × 15% ≈ 0.12 percentage points with Irish domicile, and about twice that with Luxembourg domicile.

bloecke.titel: Effect of 0.12 percentage points over 30 years
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with a lump-sum investment of €100,000 and a gross return of 6.5% before withholding tax leakage, without further costs and taxes.

bloecke.md: Synthetic ETFs on certain qualified US indices can reduce US withholding tax to zero, because US law exempts swaps on these indices from it. Evaluated product comparisons therefore show an advantage of around 0.12 to 0.26 percentage points a year over physical S&P 500 ETFs. This is offset by higher total costs, the counterparty risk of the swap partner and the possibility that the US exemption will be changed. The advantage therefore exists, but it comes at a price and is not guaranteed.

## Foreign brokers

A broker without a German paying agent, for example one based in Ireland or the Netherlands, does not withhold capital income withholding tax. This does not save the investor any tax; they merely take on the work and the risk. Under Section 32d(3) EStG, capital income that has not been subject to tax deduction must be reported in the income tax return. The assessment takes place regardless of Section 46(2) EStG. If the income is not reported, the return is incomplete. If this is done intentionally, it is tax evasion under Section 370 AO (Fiscal Code). If it is done recklessly, it is a reckless understatement of tax and thus an administrative offence (Section 378 AO). The tax office learns of the account anyway through the automatic exchange of financial account information.

The effort that investors have to make themselves is regularly underestimated.

schritte.text: Record dividends, interest, capital gains and capital losses separately, and share gains separately from all other income. The two loss offsetting groups apply here in exactly the same way, except that no bank keeps them.
Every receipt and every purchase is converted into euros at the exchange rate of the day in question, not at the annual average. The currency effect forms part of the taxable gain.
In partial sales, the units bought first are deemed to have been sold first here too. The broker's statement often follows a different method and is not decisive for tax purposes.

Calculate the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) and the partial exemption yourself. Investment fund income belongs in the investment fund income annex (Anlage KAP-INV), not in the capital income annex.
For the credit under Section 32d(5) EStG, the tax office needs proof of the foreign tax assessed and paid. Keep your dividend statements for this reason.

bloecke.md:
Under Section 149(2) AO, the return must be filed by 31 July of the following year, or by the end of February of the year after that if you are represented by a tax adviser (Section 149(3) AO). Until the tax assessment notice arrives, the tax stays in your own account. This is a genuine deferral advantage, but it involves a risk. If the money is spent, it is missing in the following year for the additional payment, especially as the tax office can then set advance payments (Section 37 EStG). It makes sense to put the estimated tax into a separate account as soon as the income is received.

The saver's allowance is not lost in this case. Without an exemption order, it is taken into account in the assessment via the capital income annex.

## Exit taxation (Wegzugsbesteuerung)

Investors who leave Germany take their portfolio with them, but not necessarily tax-free. Section 6 AStG (Foreign Tax Act) deems a sale at fair market value (gemeiner Wert) to have taken place if someone has been subject to unlimited tax liability for at least seven of the last twelve years and holds an interest of at least 1% in a corporation. The tax falls due even though no money flows. On application, it can be paid in seven equal annual instalments, as a rule only against the provision of security. If the person returns within seven years, the tax lapses, and this period can be extended by up to five years.

Ordinary share and ETF savers were long unaffected by this. Since 1 January 2025, Section 19(3) InvStG has also covered fund units held as private assets. Investors are affected if they held at least 1% of a fund in the last five years or if their acquisition costs for units in a single fund amount to at least €500,000. The threshold applies per fund, not to the entire portfolio. A portfolio built up over decades through a savings plan in a single large world ETF can exceed it, whereas the same sum spread across four funds would stay below it. How the threshold is to be interpreted in detail has not yet been conclusively clarified in the specialist literature. Advice is therefore necessary before a planned move abroad; a rule of thumb is not sufficient.

Additional costs due to a foreign connection only arise from withholding tax that cannot be credited. This means withholding tax above the treaty rate, withholding tax in a year in which no German flat-rate withholding tax is due because of an exemption order or losses, and withholding tax at fund level. The first two can be avoided, the third only through the choice of fund domicile.

The refund is handled by the tax authority of the source state, not by the German tax office. There is usually a separate form and a separate deadline, and a certificate of residence from the German tax office is also required. Switzerland uses Form 85 for this. The claim is forfeited three years after the end of the year in which the dividend fell due (Article 32 VStG, the Swiss Withholding Tax Act).

With an excess of 20 percentage points, every €1,000 of dividends brings a refund of €200. With €300 of Swiss dividends a year, the forms therefore yield €60. Service providers who take this on keep part of it as a success fee. The effort only becomes worthwhile for significant amounts. Alternatively, several years can be collected and combined in one application within the deadline.

It is simpler to cover countries with a high excess through a fund rather than through individual shares. Within the fund, the reclaim is handled institutionally.

mitnehmen: At most the rate agreed in the double taxation agreement is credited, limited to 25% per individual item of income (Section 32d(5) EStG); anything withheld beyond that can only be reclaimed in the source state.

The bank records withholding tax not yet credited in the withholding tax pot and offsets it against flat-rate withholding tax for the same year; it is lost to the extent that, because of an exemption order or losses, no German flat-rate withholding tax arises in the whole year against which it could be credited.

With funds, withholding tax has no longer been personally creditable since 2018; the partial exemption compensates for this on a flat-rate basis, and the fund domicile determines the level of withholding tax leakage.
A foreign broker does not save any tax; calculation, documentation and liability pass to the investor, who must declare the income under Section 32d(3) EStG.
Since 2025, exit taxation has also affected pure fund investors if their acquisition costs for a single fund reach €500,000.

begriffe.text: Tax withheld by the state from which income originates before the income reaches the foreign investor. Under Section 32d(5) EStG, it can be credited against German tax, but only up to the rate in the double taxation agreement and at most 25% per item of income.

Offsetting account kept by the German custodian bank for creditable foreign withholding tax that could not yet be credited. The bank offsets it against flat-rate withholding tax arising in the same year. Unlike the loss pots, the pot is not carried forward to the following year; any remainder at 31 December can only be credited in the tax return for the same year.

The part of foreign withholding tax that is incurred at fund level, reduces the net asset value without being shown separately and, since 2018, can no longer be credited to the private investor. The amount depends on the fund domicile.

Country in which the fund is based, recognisable from the prefix of the ISIN (IE, LU, DE). It determines which double taxation agreement applies to the fund and thus the withholding tax burden within the fund assets.

Deemed sale when unlimited tax liability ends under Section 6 AStG and, since 2025, for fund units also under Section 19(3) InvStG. The tax arises without a sale taking place and without any money being received.
